title: Bastion — the gateway for agent traffic
pitch: Bastion is a commercial gateway that puts a secure, authenticated, discoverable, payable machine interface in front of an existing website or API, for operators who want agents to be able to use their business without rewriting it.

refusals.title: The discovery document is derived, never hand-written
refusals.body: An operator edits one validated config. `/.well-known/agent` is computed from it — two documents describing what an org does are two documents that will disagree, and the one a stranger reads is not the one anybody edits. The origin endpoints never appear in the derived document; a test proves it.

refusals.title: Authentication is a delegation chain, not an API key
refusals.body: The caller presents delegation/1 authority and Bastion verifies it back to a root the operator trusts. Designed, not built in v0; the response says `verified: false` until the stage lands.

refusals.title: Payment is a policy, not a paywall
refusals.body: Every capability carries a price in integer minor units with a currency; pay-policy/1 decides whether the caller may be charged before the call is made. Designed, not built in v0; the response says `evaluated: false` until the stage lands.

refusals.title: Every action leaves a receipt
refusals.body: A receipt per capability call, signed by the edge, is not optional — the config validator refuses a policy that turns it off. In v0 the receipt is a stub whose outcome says the call was not made and whose signature is an unkeyed digest labelled as such.

refusals.title: The parser refuses; it does not guess
refusals.body: A non-https origin, a float price, a capability named for a department, a missing accountable human, a contact carrying mailto header separators, an unknown key without an `x-` prefix, a capability endpoint that is not on the origin's domain — each is refused with a sentence naming the field, all at once.

faq.q: What does the Bastion gateway enforce?
faq.a: A derived agent/1 discovery document that never leaks the origin, delegation/1 authentication of the caller, a pay-policy/1 decision before any charge, capability endpoints that stay on the origin's own domain, and a signed receipt per action. In this v0 skeleton stage 1 is built and tested; stages 2–4 are designed only and every response that reaches them says so.

faq.q: Where does Bastion sit in Web 4?
faq.a: It is in the Gateway layer — the "How do I connect to the old web?" question. It is a commercial product, not a protocol: it implements the open agent/1, delegation/1 and pay-policy/1 specifications and refuses to redefine any of them. Cloudflare sits in front of a site for human traffic; Bastion is that position for agent traffic.

Yes — it was measured public on 2026-09-28 while it is private-intended, and both facts are recorded in stack.json's x-note. It is a commercial product meant to stay private once it ships; the visibility on the map is what GitHub reports, not what was intended, and it stays public there until it is actually flipped.
